findings.text: reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:158 non-blocking: _ASSIGNMENT is a verbatim third copy of the repository's own shell-assignment pattern: reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:243 defines _SHELL_ASSIGNMENT with the identical regex and promotion.py:2343 already imports it as the shared owner, and reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py:127 holds ASSIGNMENT_RE. The module does not extend the owner, and two copies of 'what a program token is' can drift so that narrowing and gate-command resolution disagree on the same armed command.

reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:163 non-blocking: _VALUE_OPTIONS is a hand-maintained list and anything outside it loses its value to the positional drop. Verified by calling the reviewed module: 'pytest --cov-config coveragerc tests/test_alpha.py' narrows to ['pytest','--cov-config','tests/test_alpha.py::test_real'], so the appended id becomes the option's value and the arm collects nothing. A non-pytest program prefix goes the same way: 'env PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/x.py' narrows to ['env','-m','pytest','<id>'] and 'timeout 300 pytest tests/x.py' to ['timeout','<id>']. Each mangled arm exits non-zero with no failure id, so the new unreadable refusal catches it and no regression lands — the cost is a spurious refusal of a valid armed command, not a wrong landing.

FINDING reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:158 non-blocking: _ASSIGNMENT duplicates promotion_gate.py:243 _SHELL_ASSIGNMENT and hooks/worker_git_guard.py:127 ASSIGNMENT_RE rather than importing the shared owner, so the notion of a program token now has three copies that can drift.
FINDING reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:163 non-blocking: _VALUE_OPTIONS is hand-maintained, so an unlisted value-taking option (--cov-config) or a non-pytest program prefix (env, timeout) loses its value or argument to the positional drop; the arm then exits without a failure id and is refused as unreadable, making a valid armed command unlandable.
